external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside the system's network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.
external_entities.notes: The text does not separately model the user from the browser.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application receives browser traffic and puts jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: The background worker picks up jobs and performs the work, reading and writing the database.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue holding jobs placed by the web application and picked up by the background worker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The contents other than application log records are not specified.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the web application's settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store containing the worker's settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: talks to
data_flows.description: The browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The text does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The text does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings and queue credentials from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: read configuration
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings and database credentials from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: and the worker has a worker config. Both of those config stores hold the credentials the process needs

trust_boundaries.name: outside our network
trust_boundaries.description: The zone outside the system's network where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The browser sits outside our network

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The tier behind the web tier containing the queue, worker and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source says the browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a background worker process that picks up jobs and does work.

assumptions.assumption: The browser is in a tenant-controlled zone because it is outside the system's network and represents a user's browser.
assumptions.basis: The source says the browser sits outside our network.

assumptions.assumption: The web tier and backend tier are network boundaries because they are distinct tiers in the same system.
assumptions.basis: The source distinguishes the web tier from the backend tier by network-tier placement.

assumptions.assumption: The backend tier is a network boundary because it is a distinct tier behind the web tier in the same system.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the queue, worker and database as being in the backend tier behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config contains confidential data because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web application config holds the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config contains confidential data because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source says the worker config holds the worker's database credentials.
